searchData.title: What is Budgeting?
searchData.description: Budgeting is the process of planning how you will use your income for expenses, savings, and other financial needs.

searchData.title: What is a Need?
searchData.description: A need is something essential for daily life, such as food, basic clothing, education, and necessary transportation.

searchData.title: What is a Want?
searchData.description: A want is something you would like to have but can live without, such as entertainment, luxury items, or unnecessary shopping.

searchData.title: 50-30-20 Budget Rule
searchData.description: The 50-30-20 rule is an educational budgeting guideline that suggests 50% for needs, 30% for wants, and 20% for savings.

searchData.title: Savings Goals
searchData.description: A savings goal defines how much money you want to save, how much you already have, and how much you plan to contribute each month.

searchData.title: How to Avoid Overspending
searchData.description: Planning expenses, tracking small purchases, and separating needs from wants can help reduce unnecessary spending.

searchData.title: Impulse Buying
searchData.description: Impulse buying means purchasing something without planning or considering whether it is actually needed.

searchData.title: Small Expenses
searchData.description: Small daily expenses can add up over time, so tracking them can help you understand where your money goes.

searchData.title: Expense Planner
searchData.description: The Expense Planner allows users to add sample expenses, view planned spending, and calculate the remaining sample balance.

searchData.title: Saving Tips
searchData.description: Set a clear savings goal, track your progress, and regularly contribute an amount that fits your budget.
